keyVerseText: And Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second: but Jeush and Beriah had not many sons; therefore they were in one reckoning, according to their father's house. had: Heb. did not multiply sons
rootMeaning: The root word זִיזָא (Zîyzâʼ) means "shining," suggesting a sense of brightness or radiance. זִיזָה (Zîyzâh) is an alternative form of this root and carries the connotation of "abundance," which extends the idea of shining to imply fullness or plentifulness. This etymology enriches the English gloss by connecting the name to qualities of vibrancy and flourishing, rather than merely being a proper name.
usageInScripture: The word זִיזָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 23:11, where it is used as a proper name referring to a Gershonite Levite. The top translation reflects this personal name usage with the phrase "and Zizah." This consistency in translation as a proper name indicates that its primary scriptural function is to identify a specific individual rather than to convey a conceptual meaning.
theologicalSignificance: Though זִיזָה is used as a proper name, its root meaning of "shining" and "abundance" invites reflection on the character and role of God's servants. As a Levite, Zizah represents those called to minister in the house of the Lord, embodying the radiance and fruitfulness that come from faithful service. This reminds believers that God’s people are called to shine with His glory and to abound in spiritual fruitfulness. The name thus symbolizes how God’s grace enables His servants to reflect His light and multiply His blessings within His covenant community.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 23:11, the verse notes that Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second, highlighting Zizah’s position among the Levites. The mention of Zizah here as the second son underscores his role within the priestly lineage, contributing to the organization of the Levitical families. The name’s connotation of "abundance" and "shining" enriches this verse by suggesting that Zizah’s place in the community was marked by a distinguished and fruitful ministry, even as the verse notes the limited number of sons in related families.
